newsitem.title: USA: Murphy seeks alliances for U.S. refineries.
newsitem.headline: Murphy seeks alliances for U.S. refineries.

text.p: Murphy Oil Corp is seeking "alliances" for its U.S. oil refining operations, a company official said Wednesday.
Murphy was cited by a senior Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) official on Tuesday as one of several U.S. companies it was in talks with for potential downstream deals.

"Just like everyone else in the industry we're looking for strategic alliances," said Fred Green, manager of refinery operations and crude oil supply for the El Dorado, Ark., based company, although he declined to comment specifically on talks with PdVSA.
In the U.S., Murphy operates a 95,000 barrel per day (bpd) refinery in Meraux, Louisiana and 36,000 bpd plant in Superior, Wisconsin.
Green also preferred to remain vague on whether the company was in talks with other oil-producing countries, apart from PDVSA, but said the company was considering all options.
"We have done business with all the Latin American producers," though the company has no long-term deals with suppliers, he noted.
In March, Murphy withdrew from a proposed merger that would have linked its U.K. subsidiary Murco Petroleum Ltd with the downstream U.K. operations of Elf Aquitaine and Chevron Corp.

Murphy chief executive Claiborne Deming told shareholders that the company was still looking for an alliance and said U.S. downstream operations "similarly are competing in difficult market conditions."

The only publically announced U.S. downstream initiative is a study this year of a project with Wal-Mart to construct high-volume gasoline stations. Murphy operates about 500 retail outlets, either under the Spur brand or through contracters, spread around the southern and upper midwestern U.S. Two of the Wal-Mart sites are currently running out of a total of 20 or more that are planned.
Murphy's downstream assets might prove a good fit for PDVSA, which has been among the most agressive buyers of downstream assets in the U.S., analysts said.

PDVSA currently has about 560,000 barrels per day refining capacity through its Citgo subsidiary. The company expects to close a deal next month to buy out from Unocal Corp the remaining 50 percent stake in the UNO-VEN joint venture, including a 153,000 bpd refinery in Lemont, Illinois. It also increased its stake earlier this year with Lyondell Petrochemical Corp's 265,000 bpd Houston plant.

Murphy is typical of the smaller to mid-sized U.S. integrated oil companies looking to free up capital employed in poorly performing downstream assets so as to concentrate on exploration and development.
Murphy reported 1996 net earnings of $137.8 million, of which $124 million came from exploration and production and just $14 million from worldwide refining and marketing.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
